project.name: chat-analyzer-pro
project.description: Analyzes WhatsApp and Telegram chat exports from the terminal, producing message statistics, sentiment, relationship, and network insights in a single self-contained HTML report. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: __main__.py
nodes.summary: Python module entry point enabling `python -m chat_analyzer`; raises SystemExit with the Typer app from the cli package.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: CLI package init exposing the Typer `app` as the console-script (D-01) target; importing the package pulls only typer and the standard library.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: Typer CLI for chat-analyzer: validates WhatsApp/Telegram export paths, resolves the NLP tier via an interactive menu or env override, and orchestrates the analysis pipeline, HTML report generation, and report opening with friendly, never-traceback errors.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy analysis modules are imported lazily inside `_analyze_path` so that `--help`/`--version` stay instant.

nodes.name: nlp_gate.py
nodes.summary: Environment gate for the optional NLP extras: verifies pinned package versions and cached Hugging Face models, exposes tier knobs (emotion sample cap, worker count, result cache), and installs/updates packages or downloads models, with a Windows long-path guard around pip and model cache paths.
nodes.languageNotes: Centralizes all behavior knobs as environment-variable parsers with validation and safe defaults, so downstream stages never crash on malformed env values.

nodes.name: result_cache.py
nodes.summary: Disk-backed JSON result cache: derives a deterministic key from the chat file hash, app version, and NLP/sampling configuration; stores sanitized pipeline results atomically with TTL pruning and treats corrupt or schema-mismatched entries as cache misses.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a temp-file-plus-`os.replace` write pattern for atomic, crash-safe cache updates.

nodes.name: _friendly_error
nodes.summary: Builds user-facing failure lines that pair the error cause with inline WhatsApp/Telegram export instructions (D-14) instead of tracebacks, covering missing files, unsupported extensions, and empty chats.

nodes.name: _version_callback
nodes.summary: Eager Typer callback implementing the `--version` flag (typer 0.27 has no built-in version option), printing the package version and exiting.

nodes.name: _tier_menu
nodes.summary: Renders the interactive three-option NLP tier menu (basic / lean / full) and returns the chosen tier as an int.

nodes.name: _tier_from_env
nodes.summary: Reads the NLP tier from the CHAT_ANALYZER_TIER environment override for non-interactive runs, falling back to tier 1 silently.

nodes.name: _announce_install
nodes.summary: Prints the notice shown before NLP package/model installation begins, mentioning CPU-only mode when applicable.

nodes.name: _ensure_nlp_for_tier
nodes.summary: Brings the chosen NLP tier ready before analysis: checks nlp_gate status, installs and updates packages and downloads models on first run, and prompts interactively when the install is outdated or a Windows long-path issue blocks it.

nodes.name: _analyze_path
nodes.summary: Runs the full pipeline for one validated export (lazily importing the heavy analysis modules), prints the once-per-run message count, writes the HTML report, and opens it.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Typer command handler: validates the positional chat path (with friendly re-prompt loop when interactive), reconfigures UTF-8 stdout/stderr, resolves the NLP tier via menu or env, then dispatches to _analyze_path with graceful error exits.

nodes.name: model_cached
nodes.summary: Checks whether a Hugging Face model directory exists in the local hub cache for the given model id.

nodes.name: emotion_sample_cap
nodes.summary: Parses the emotion sampling cap from its environment variable, returning None for 'off', the documented default when absent or garbage, and never raising on malformed input.

nodes.name: emotion_worker_count
nodes.summary: Resolves the emotion-analysis parallel worker count from its environment variable, clamping between 1 and CPU count so malformed values degrade to sequential.

nodes.name: result_cache_enabled
nodes.summary: Parses the opt-in flag that enables the disk result cache, treating the environment variable as truthy only for explicit on-values.

nodes.name: result_cache_dir
nodes.summary: Resolves the result cache directory, returning None when the cache is disabled, honoring an explicit env path, and otherwise defaulting to LOCALAPPDATA or the user home.

nodes.name: nlp_available
nodes.summary: Reports whether NLP is usable for a given model id, honoring the force-off env override and verifying the model is present in the local cache.

nodes.name: nlp_installed_versions
nodes.summary: Collects the installed versions of the pinned NLP packages via importlib.metadata, reporting None for absent packages.

nodes.name: nlp_versions_satisfied
nodes.summary: Compares installed package versions against the declared version pins using packaging SpecifierSet.

nodes.name: nlp_models_cached
nodes.summary: Returns True only when both required models (emotion classifier and summarizer) are present in the local Hugging Face cache.

nodes.name: nlp_status
nodes.summary: Aggregates package-install, version-pin, and model-cache checks into a single readiness status dict consumed by the CLI tier flow.

nodes.name: _pip_install
nodes.summary: Runs pip install/upgrade as a subprocess with output capture, raising a friendly RuntimeError that surfaces the captured output on failure.

nodes.name: registry_long_paths_enabled
nodes.summary: Reads the Windows registry (LongPathsEnabled) to determine whether long-path support is active, failing safe to False on non-Windows or missing keys.

nodes.name: windows_long_path_message
nodes.summary: Returns a corrective message when a target path would exceed the Windows MAX_PATH limit and long-path support is off, honoring the CHAT_ANALYZER_ALLOW_LONG_PATH override.

nodes.name: install_nlp
nodes.summary: Installs the pinned NLP packages via pip (optionally CPU-only torch) after applying the Windows long-path guard.

nodes.name: update_nlp
nodes.summary: Upgrades already-installed NLP packages to the pinned versions after applying the Windows long-path guard.

nodes.name: download_models
nodes.summary: Downloads the pinned Hugging Face models (emotion classifier and summarizer) into the local cache via snapshot_download, raising a friendly RuntimeError when huggingface_hub is missing or the download fails.

nodes.name: sha256_file
nodes.summary: Streams a file in chunks to compute its SHA-256 digest, used as the content fingerprint in the cache key.

nodes.name: _app_version
nodes.summary: Best-effort lookup of the installed package version, used to invalidate cache entries after an app upgrade.

nodes.name: cache_key
nodes.summary: Builds a deterministic SHA-256 cache key from the chat file hash, app version, NLP on/off, sample cap, worker count, and sorted chosen transcripts.

nodes.name: _sanitize
nodes.summary: Recursively converts numpy/pandas scalars and arrays, NaN/Inf floats, and nested containers into JSON-serializable primitives so pipeline results can be cached safely.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Reads and validates a cached result JSON, deleting corrupt entries and treating schema mismatches, wrong app versions, or missing fields as a cache miss.

nodes.name: store
nodes.summary: Writes sanitized pipeline results to the cache atomically (temp file plus os.replace) after TTL pruning, cleaning up the temp file on failure.

nodes.name: _prune
nodes.summary: Deletes cache entries older than the configured max age (default 30 days) so the cache directory cannot grow unbounded.

nodes.name: adapters.py
nodes.summary: Adapts the analysis modules' raw result dicts (EDA, sentiment, charts, health, network, emotion, narrative) into the typed AnalysisResults contract consumed by the CLI pipeline and HTML report, and generates human-readable insight strings via build_insights. Acts as the single anti-corruption layer that knows each module's internal dict shape, with defensive .get() access so empty edge-case dicts never raise.
nodes.languageNotes: Every access is a defensive .get() with `or {}` fallbacks, so sparse analysis results degrade to neutral values instead of raising KeyError; documented as 'Research Pattern 2' in the module docstring.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the utilities subpackage that re-exports the text preprocessing helpers and the ChatVisualizer class with an explicit __all__ list.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package __init__ barrel using an explicit __all__ to expose only four public names (ChatVisualizer, clean_messages, extract_emojis, preprocess_text).

nodes.name: preprocessing.py
nodes.summary: Text preprocessing utilities for chat analysis: message cleaning, emoji and URL extraction, simple tokenization, question detection, and non-Latin-script share measurement that powers the honesty disclaimer in the CLI report.
nodes.languageNotes: Emoji handling is based on hand-rolled Unicode-range regexes (no emoji library dependency), keeping the package lean but bound to the ranges compiled into the pattern.

nodes.name: visualization.py
nodes.summary: Matplotlib-based visualization suite: the ChatVisualizer class renders timelines, day-hour heatmaps, word clouds, emoji distributions, sentiment plots, response-time histograms, health trends and a multi-panel summary dashboard, plus module-level quick_* convenience wrappers.
nodes.languageNotes: Every plotting entry point fails soft: it logs and returns None instead of raising, so a plotting failure never aborts the CLI pipeline; the module attaches logging.NullHandler instead of configuring global logging.

nodes.name: adapt
nodes.summary: Central adapter that assembles raw analysis dicts into the typed AnalysisResults contract: computes participant stats, content frequencies, sentiment aggregates and time-range scalars, then delegates to the health/network/emotion/narrative block builders before constructing the final result object.

nodes.name: _build_health_block
nodes.summary: Extracts relationship-health scalars (score, components, initiator ratio, response patterns and dominance stats) into a normalized health block with safe defaults.

nodes.name: _strongest_connection_summary
nodes.summary: Formats the top two network edges into a human-readable 'strongest connection' sentence for the report insights, falling back to a neutral message when the network is empty.

nodes.name: _build_network_block
nodes.summary: Normalizes network analysis output (node/edge counts, centrality metrics, interaction patterns and the strongest-connection summary) into the network block of the results contract.

nodes.name: _build_emotion_block
nodes.summary: Normalizes emotion analysis output (dominant-emotion distribution and sample coverage) into the emotion block with safe defaults for empty results.

nodes.name: _build_narrative_block
nodes.summary: Converts narrative-analysis observations into display-ready strings and flags (arc signal, sensitive-topic driver, tier-B lead) for the report's narrative tab.

nodes.name: build_insights
nodes.summary: Generates the human-readable insight list shown in the CLI summary and HTML report: activity leaders, message volume, word/emoji usage, sentiment balance, relationship health, network connectivity, emotion mix, and non-Latin-script disclaimers.

nodes.name: preprocess_text
nodes.summary: Cleans a single chat message for analysis: strips URLs and mentions, optionally lowercases, and collapses whitespace.

nodes.name: clean_messages
nodes.summary: DataFrame-level cleaner that drops null and below-minimum-length messages, strips whitespace, and removes '<Media omitted>' placeholders before analysis.

nodes.name: extract_emojis
nodes.summary: Extracts all emoji codepoints from a message using a compiled Unicode-range regex.

nodes.name: remove_emojis
nodes.summary: Removes emoji codepoints from a message using the shared Unicode-range regex.

nodes.name: extract_urls
nodes.summary: Finds http/https URLs in a message with a regular expression.

nodes.name: tokenize_simple
nodes.summary: Splits a message into raw word tokens on whitespace as a dependency-free tokenizer.

nodes.name: count_words
nodes.summary: Counts the words in a message via the simple whitespace tokenizer.

nodes.name: normalize_whitespace
nodes.summary: Collapses repeated whitespace characters and trims a string to a single-spaced form.

nodes.name: contains_question
nodes.summary: Detects whether a message is a question via a '?' character or an interrogative-word prefix such as what, why, how, do or are.

nodes.name: is_short_response
nodes.summary: Returns True when a message is at most the threshold character count, used to flag quick acknowledgements.

nodes.name: is_non_latin_heavy
nodes.summary: Checks whether the share of non-Latin, non-emoji codepoints in a message exceeds a ratio threshold, powering the analysis-honesty disclaimer path.

nodes.name: non_latin_message_share
nodes.summary: Computes the fraction of DataFrame messages that are non-Latin-heavy, surfaced in the CLI report as a disclaimer metric via the adapters layer.

nodes.name: ChatVisualizer
nodes.summary: Matplotlib figure factory for chat analysis: one plotting method per chart type (message timeline, day-hour activity heatmap, word cloud, emoji distribution, sentiment pie and timeline, user activity, response-time histogram, relationship-health trend) plus a five-panel summary dashboard; every method fails soft, returning None and logging instead of raising.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Initializes the figure size and plot style, applying the shared seaborn palette for all subsequent charts.

nodes.name: plot_message_timeline
nodes.summary: Plots the messages-per-period time series resampled from the timestamp index, with an optional polynomial trend line overlaid.

nodes.name: plot_activity_heatmap
nodes.summary: Renders a day-of-week by hour activity heatmap with weekday rows reindexed into calendar order.

nodes.name: plot_wordcloud
nodes.summary: Generates a word cloud from the concatenated message text with configurable stopwords, size and colormap, failing soft to a placeholder figure when no text is available.

nodes.name: plot_emoji_distribution
nodes.summary: Extracts emojis from every message and renders a horizontal bar chart of the most common emoji with count labels.

nodes.name: plot_sentiment_distribution
nodes.summary: Renders a pie chart of positive, negative and neutral message counts with bold percentage labels.

nodes.name: plot_sentiment_timeline
nodes.summary: Plots the resampled average sentiment score over time with a centered 7-point rolling mean and a neutral baseline at zero.

nodes.name: plot_user_activity
nodes.summary: Draws a horizontal bar chart of message counts per participant, showing the top-N most active senders with count labels.

nodes.name: plot_response_time_distribution
nodes.summary: Histograms the inter-message response times with a vertical line marking the median response speed.

nodes.name: plot_relationship_health_trend
nodes.summary: Plots the resampled relationship-health score over time as a filled area with good and caution threshold lines.

nodes.name: create_summary_dashboard
nodes.summary: Composes a five-panel matplotlib dashboard (daily volume, top participants, sentiment pie, hourly activity, weekday activity) and saves it to disk when given an output path.

nodes.name: quick_timeline
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that constructs a ChatVisualizer and plots the message timeline in a single call.

nodes.name: quick_heatmap
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that constructs a ChatVisualizer and plots the activity heatmap in a single call.

nodes.name: quick_wordcloud
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that constructs a ChatVisualizer and plots a word cloud in a single call.

nodes.name: quick_sentiment
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that constructs a ChatVisualizer and plots the sentiment distribution in a single call.

nodes.name: quick_dashboard
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that constructs a ChatVisualizer and saves the summary dashboard in a single call.

nodes.name: chart_json.py
nodes.summary: Builds JSON-serializable ECharts chart specifications for the offline HTML report — daily timeline, activity heatmap, participant bars, sentiment trend, health trend, and a 3D network layout — plus emotion pie and quarterly-timeline specs.
nodes.languageNotes: All numeric values pass through _float_or_none so NumPy scalars and NaN become JSON-safe floats or None before being embedded in the report.

nodes.name: pipeline.py
nodes.summary: Orchestrates a full analysis run: detects the input type (WhatsApp, Telegram, or ZIP), parses it into the canonical DataFrame, then drives EDA, sentiment, relationship-health, network, chart-spec, narrative, emotion, and Tier-B summarization stages before mapping results into the AnalysisResults contract.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy NLP modules (emotion, summarizer, sentiment) are imported lazily inside run_pipeline so the lean base install stays fast and parse-only runs avoid loading transformers.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the ingest layer, re-exporting get_dependency_status, get_supported_formats, and process_uploaded_file via an explicit __all__ so callers import the ingestion API directly from chat_analyzer.ingest.

nodes.name: ingestion.py
nodes.summary: Handles every supported input format — WhatsApp .txt exports, Telegram-style JSON, ZIP archives, screenshots (OCR), PDFs (pdfplumber with OCR fallback), and media attachments — normalizing raw messages into the canonical message schema and DataFrame with honest skip counting.
nodes.languageNotes: Optional parsers (pytesseract, pdfplumber) are guarded with try/except and logged warnings, so missing native binaries degrade to empty results instead of crashing the run.

nodes.name: build_chart_specs
nodes.summary: Aggregates the six base chart specs (timeline, activity, participants, sentiment, health, network) into a single JSON-serializable dict for the HTML report, degrading to an empty spec set on failure.

nodes.name: build_emotion_spec
nodes.summary: Builds the emotion-distribution pie spec (top emotions with dominant-emotion share) from an emotion summary, returning None when no distribution is present.

nodes.name: build_emotion_timeline_spec
nodes.summary: Builds a quarterly emotion line-chart spec, emitting one series per emotion with None-safe floats for missing or malformed quarterly entries.

nodes.name: _build_timeline
nodes.summary: Resamples message timestamps to a per-day count series for the timeline chart.

nodes.name: _build_activity
nodes.summary: Builds the day-of-week by hour activity heatmap cells from message timestamps, including axis labels and peak-total metadata.

nodes.name: _build_participants
nodes.summary: Builds the participant bar-chart spec with message counts and share percentages per sender.

nodes.name: _build_sentiment
nodes.summary: Builds the daily sentiment trend spec with raw daily VADER means and a 7-day rolling average from compound scores.

nodes.name: _build_health
nodes.summary: Builds the relationship-health trend line spec from the rolling health DataFrame, skipping rows with unparseable dates.

nodes.name: _build_network
nodes.summary: Converts the NetworkX interaction graph into a 3D ECharts network spec with spring-layout coordinates, node sizes by degree, edge widths by weight, and highlight metadata for the strongest pair.

nodes.name: _float_or_none
nodes.summary: Coerces arbitrary values to JSON-safe floats, mapping NaN and non-numeric input to None.

nodes.name: fig_to_data_uri
nodes.summary: Renders a Matplotlib figure to a base64 PNG data URI for embedding in the HTML report and closes the figure to free memory.

nodes.name: _safe_chart
nodes.summary: Wraps a chart-building callable so any exception is logged and degrades to None instead of aborting the report build.

nodes.name: stage_status
nodes.summary: Wraps a pipeline stage in a Rich status spinner on interactive consoles and a plain context manager otherwise.

nodes.name: stage
nodes.summary: Advances the Rich progress bar and shows a stage spinner while a named pipeline stage runs.

nodes.name: _tier_b_digest
nodes.summary: Assembles a deterministic fallback digest from narrative observations plus chat stats (participants, message count) when the Tier-B summarizer is unavailable.

nodes.name: _acceptable_narrative_text
nodes.summary: Validates that a narrative summary is non-empty, within the length cap, and free of error-message markers.

nodes.name: run_pipeline
nodes.summary: Runs the complete analysis pipeline end to end: input-type dispatch and parsing, canonical DataFrame construction, EDA, sentiment, relationship health, network analysis, chart specs, narrative synthesis, emotion analysis, Tier-B summarization with digest fallback, adapter mapping, and optional result caching.

nodes.name: get_dependency_status
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the optional-dependency status map describing which parsers are available.

nodes.name: try_parse_datetime
nodes.summary: Parses WhatsApp date/time strings across common formats including AM/PM and zero-padded variants, returning an ISO string or None.

nodes.name: parse_whatsapp_text
nodes.summary: Parses raw WhatsApp export text line by line against WAP_MESSAGE_RE, attaching multi-line continuations and collecting skipped header lines honestly.

nodes.name: parse_json_chat
nodes.summary: Parses Telegram-style chat JSON from str, bytes, or file-like input, flattening supported message shapes into raw message dicts and warning on malformed payloads.

nodes.name: ocr_image_bytes
nodes.summary: Runs Tesseract OCR over image bytes and returns the extracted text, degrading to empty on failure.

nodes.name: extract_text_from_pdf
nodes.summary: Extracts per-page text with pdfplumber and falls back to page-level OCR for scanned PDFs, joining pages with blank-line separators.

nodes.name: _ocr_pdf_page
nodes.summary: Rasterizes a single PDF page and OCRs it with Tesseract.

nodes.name: extract_media_metadata
nodes.summary: Builds a metadata dict (kind, extension, human-readable size) for a media attachment.

nodes.name: _format_file_size
nodes.summary: Formats a byte count as a human-readable KB/MB size string.

nodes.name: _to_naive_utc
nodes.summary: Normalizes datetimes and ISO strings to naive UTC timestamps so all downstream analysis operates on one timezone convention.

nodes.name: messages_to_dataframe
nodes.summary: Converts raw message dicts into the canonical pandas DataFrame (timestamp, sender, message, day, word_count, id), dropping unparseable rows and optionally returning honest skip counts.

nodes.name: normalize_message
nodes.summary: Normalizes one raw message dict into the canonical schema with id, timestamp, sender, text, media fields, and honest defaults for missing parts.

nodes.name: _read_file_content
nodes.summary: Reads bytes from an uploaded file-like object or filesystem path, raising ValueError for unsupported sources.

nodes.name: process_uploaded_file
nodes.summary: Routes an uploaded file by extension to the format-specific processor and returns normalized messages, skipped-row counts, and media metadata.

nodes.name: _process_zip_file
nodes.summary: Walks a ZIP archive member by member, parsing transcript members and cataloguing media and unsupported members honestly.

nodes.name: _process_text_file
nodes.summary: Decodes .txt content and parses it as a WhatsApp transcript.

nodes.name: _process_json_file
nodes.summary: Parses .json content as a chat export into raw messages.

nodes.name: _process_image_file
nodes.summary: OCRs an image attachment into a pseudo-message and records its media metadata.

nodes.name: _process_pdf_file
nodes.summary: Extracts text from a PDF attachment into a pseudo-message and records its media metadata.

nodes.name: _process_media_file
nodes.summary: Records metadata for audio/video media members without transcription.

nodes.name: _process_unknown_file
nodes.summary: Best-effort handling of unknown members: attempts WhatsApp parsing, else records the member as unsupported.

nodes.name: get_supported_formats
nodes.summary: Lists the transcript, image, PDF, and media extensions the ingestion layer supports.

nodes.name: contracts.py
nodes.summary: Defines the CLI pipeline's interface contracts: the ParseReport dataclass aggregating parse counters and the AnalysisResults TypedDict describing the complete analysis payload shared by pipeline, adapters, render, and report_html while keeping the analysis core CLI-agnostic.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a plain @dataclass for runtime parse counters and a TypedDict for the dict-shaped analysis payload, giving static typing without runtime overhead; the analysis core never imports this module.

nodes.name: render.py
nodes.summary: Thin terminal narration layer that renders the end-of-run summary panel (totals, participants, date range, report path) plus NLP-status, emotion-sampling, and narrative 'What's going on' lines from AnalysisResults using Rich, restricted to ASCII-safe output.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately ASCII-only rendering ([WARN]/[INFO] prefixes, ASCII box style, no emoji) so output survives terminals without UTF-8 support; owns no business logic and reads AnalysisResults only.

nodes.name: report_html.py
nodes.summary: Renders the single self-contained HTML report card: an autoescape Jinja2 template with tabbed panels, boundary-validated chart PNG data URIs and interactive ECharts specs, inline-scrubbed vendored ECharts bundles, a sanitized report filename written to the cwd, and best-effort browser auto-open.
nodes.languageNotes: Security-hardened rendering: chat content is treated as untrusted input with Jinja autoescape enforced explicitly, inlined JS is scrubbed of script-terminating sequences (</script, <!--), filenames are sanitized cross-platform, and non-JSON-serializable chart specs degrade to PNG fallbacks instead of emitting broken JS.

nodes.name: ParseReport
nodes.summary: Dataclass aggregating parse counters for one export file: source path, total lines, parsed messages, skipped lines, system messages, and media messages.

nodes.name: AnalysisResults
nodes.summary: TypedDict describing the complete analysis payload produced by run_pipeline: parse/stats/participants/content/sentiment scalars, health and network blocks, narrative, gated emotion block (None when NLP is unavailable), PNG charts and interactive charts_json, insights, and report_path.

nodes.name: show_summary
nodes.summary: Prints the end-of-run terminal summary: skip/system warnings, an ASCII summary panel with totals, participants and date range, the report path, an NLP-availability status line, an emotion sampling note, and the narrative 'What's going on' lead.

nodes.name: _inline_js
nodes.summary: Neutralizes strings that would terminate or comment out an inline <script> element by escaping </script and <!-- in any JavaScript inlined into the report.

nodes.name: _load_inline_asset
nodes.summary: Loads a vendored ECharts bundle from the package assets via importlib.resources, scrubs script-terminating sequences, and degrades to an empty string when the asset is missing so the report still renders with PNG charts.

nodes.name: sanitize_filename
nodes.summary: Sanitizes a report filename stem for cross-platform safety by stripping Windows-invalid characters, path separators, and control characters, falling back to 'chat_analysis' when the result is empty.

nodes.name: _json_serializable
nodes.summary: Boundary guard returning True only when a value round-trips through json.dumps with allow_nan=False, so NaN or numpy-typed chart specs are dropped before reaching the template.

nodes.name: _validate_charts_json
nodes.summary: Boundary-validates the interactive ECharts specs, keeping only dict and JSON-serializable specs per chart key and degrading invalid entries to empty specs so their PNG fallback renders instead.

nodes.name: write_report
nodes.summary: Renders the self-contained HTML report via the autoescape Jinja template: validates chart data URIs and specs at the boundary, fills the narrative lead based on Tier A/Tier B status, inlines scrubbed ECharts bundles, and writes <sanitized-stem>_report.html to the current working directory.

nodes.name: open_report
nodes.summary: Best-effort auto-open of the report in the default browser, honoring the CHAT_ANALYZER_NO_OPEN=1 opt-out and returning False without crashing when opening fails.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the parser module that re-exports parse_telegram_chat and parse_whatsapp_chat so callers can import both platform parsers from one namespace.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package __init__ using an explicit __all__ list to constrain the public surface of the parser package.

nodes.name: telegram_parser.py
nodes.summary: Parses Telegram chat exports in both bare-chat and full-export JSON shapes, recursively joining entity-array message texts, filtering service messages, normalizing tz-aware dates to naive UTC, and returning a DataFrame plus an honest drop report.

nodes.name: whatsapp_parser.py
nodes.summary: Line-oriented WhatsApp export parser that regex-matches both bracketed and plain timestamp layouts, classifies system and media lines with honest counters, and enriches the resulting DataFrame with word, emoji, media, and time-period features.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a compiled fixed-shape fast path for canonical WhatsApp timestamps with a strptime fallback over 16 date formats; DD/MM is tried before MM/DD to avoid silently misreading dates when day <= 12.

nodes.name: _load_messages
nodes.summary: Extracts the message list from either a bare chat export's top-level 'messages' key or each chat inside a full export's 'chats' array, raising ValueError for unknown shapes instead of silently returning empty data.

nodes.name: _join_text
nodes.summary: Recursively flattens Telegram entity-array text parts — plain strings, nested entities, and links — into a single concatenated message string.

nodes.name: _to_naive_utc
nodes.summary: Converts a Telegram ISO date string into a timezone-naive UTC datetime so both platform parsers share one timestamp convention.

nodes.name: parse_telegram_chat_with_report
nodes.summary: Reads a Telegram export from a URL or local JSON path, iterates messages, joins entity text, drops service messages, and returns normalized message rows together with a report counting total versus dropped messages.

nodes.name: parse_telegram_chat
nodes.summary: Public convenience wrapper that runs parse_telegram_chat_with_report and returns only the normalized messages DataFrame, discarding the drop report.

nodes.name: WhatsAppParser
nodes.summary: Parses WhatsApp .txt exports line by line with strict datetime parsing and dual message regexes, classifies headerless system lines and the encryption notice with honest skip counters, and enriches the DataFrame with word counts, emoji counts, media flags, and time-period categories.
nodes.languageNotes: Holds five compiled regexes (message, alt bracket format, system header, system phrase, encryption notice) as instance state across 11 methods covering strict/fast datetime parsing, report-based parsing, feature enrichment, persistence, and stats.

nodes.name: parse_whatsapp_chat
nodes.summary: Scripted entry point that parses a WhatsApp export via WhatsAppParser, optionally saves the processed CSV, and prints basic conversation statistics to stdout.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions CI workflow that runs three parallel jobs — a lean pytest matrix across ubuntu/windows and Python 3.11/3.12, a slow CLI/e2e suite with a ruff lint pass, and an NLP job proving the optional [nlp] extra installs — with in-progress runs on the same ref cancelled.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses an OS/Python matrix strategy with fail-fast disabled, per-ref concurrency cancellation, and pip dependency caching configured through setup-python.

nodes.name: test
nodes.summary: Matrix job over ubuntu-latest/windows-latest and Python 3.11/3.12 that installs the base package with dev extras and runs the lean pytest suite (slow tests deselected) while enforcing a 50% branch-coverage floor.

nodes.name: slow

nodes.name: emotion.py
nodes.summary: Six-class emotion classification (joy, sadness, anger, fear, surprise, love) via a HuggingFace DistilBERT pipeline, with deterministic stratified sampling above the 50k-message cap, process-pool parallel exact scoring, opt-in INT8 quantization, quarterly timelines, and plotting helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Sampling is reproducible by design: largest-remainder seats per sender across ~50 time buckets with random_state=42; unscored rows keep neutral 1/6 scores and the frame gains an emotion_scored column plus an emotion_sample attrs dict.

nodes.name: _score_text_chunk
nodes.summary: Worker function that scores a chunk of texts through an emotion pipeline — sizing torch threads from the environment, applying optional quantization, and returning per-text label/score dicts with per-chunk error containment so one bad batch never kills the run.

nodes.name: _maybe_quantize_pipeline
nodes.summary: Applies opt-in dynamic INT8 quantization to the emotion model when CHAT_ANALYZER_EMOTION_QUANT is enabled, degrading silently to fp32 if quantization fails.

nodes.name: _allocate_seats
nodes.summary: Largest-remainder seat allocator that distributes a sample cap proportionally across senders, clamping to available message counts for deterministic stratified sampling.

nodes.name: _global_time_edges
nodes.summary: Computes the global earliest/latest scorable timestamps and ~50 equal time-bucket edges used to stratify the emotion sample across the chat's timeline.

nodes.name: _pick_in_sender
nodes.summary: Selects which of a single sender's messages get scored by distributing that sender's seats across time buckets deterministically, returning the chosen row indices with random_state=42 draws.

nodes.name: _stratified_sample_indices
nodes.summary: Builds the deterministic stratified sample across all senders by combining per-sender seat allocation with time-bucket picks, returning the sampled indices plus sample metadata for the emotion_sample attrs dict.

nodes.name: _parse_emotion_scores
nodes.summary: Normalizes raw pipeline result dictionaries into a uniform {label: score} mapping aligned to the six emotion labels.

nodes.name: EmotionAnalyzer

nodes.languageNotes: Every observation text opens with a hedge ('Possibly', 'May', 'Might') except the always-present factual snapshot; Banglish keyword lexicons match whole tokens only, never substrings.

nodes.name: _ascii_safe
nodes.summary: Strips non-ASCII characters from derived values so narrative output never carries raw chat text or emoji downstream.

nodes.name: _normalize
nodes.summary: Coerces the input frame into the narrative module's expected shape: filled sender/message values and computed message_length as a numeric column.

nodes.name: _confidence
nodes.summary: Maps a signal score plus sample size to a conservative confidence level from a documented table, damping confidence for small samples.

nodes.name: _message_length_asymmetry
nodes.summary: Detects one-sided verbosity by comparing per-sender mean message lengths, producing the asymmetry signal that feeds engagement and driver observations.

nodes.name: _question_ratio_per_sender
nodes.summary: Computes per-sender question-mark ratios and totals to identify who drives the conversation with questions, feeding the driver signal.

nodes.name: _reciprocity
nodes.summary: Measures turn-taking balance between participants as the reciprocity signal for the narrative layer.

nodes.name: _sensitive_topic_driver
nodes.summary: Scans messages for care/trust and planning Banglish keyword hits (whole-token matches only) to identify sensitive-topic drivers between participants.

nodes.name: _arc_signal
nodes.summary: Classifies the conversation arc (casual vs planning/decision) from keyword trends across message windows.

nodes.name: _snapshot_observation
nodes.summary: Builds the always-present, never-hedged factual snapshot observation (message and sender counts, timespan) that anchors the narrative output.

nodes.name: _build_observations
nodes.summary: Assembles the final hedged observation list from all Tier A signals with stable kind labels and conservative confidence levels, appending the snapshot baseline first.

nodes.name: analyze_narrative
nodes.summary: Public entry point that normalizes the frame, computes all Tier A signals, and returns the narrative payload with a status block reporting that only the Tier A heuristic path ran.

nodes.name: network_graph.py

nodes.name: build_interaction_network
nodes.summary: Builds a weighted directed NetworkX graph from consecutive-message sender transitions, pre-adding all participants as nodes and applying an optional edge-weight threshold.

nodes.name: calculate_network_metrics
nodes.summary: Computes node/edge counts, density, degree/in-degree/out-degree centrality, betweenness, PageRank, and weak/strong connectivity with diameter diagnostics for the interaction graph.

nodes.name: identify_key_participants
nodes.summary: Ranks hubs (highest degree), bridges (betweenness), and influencers (PageRank) into a key-participant summary identifying who dominates the conversation network.

nodes.name: analyze_interaction_patterns
nodes.summary: Extracts strongest interaction pairs, reciprocal dyads, directionality imbalance, and pattern observations from the graph's edge weights.

nodes.name: detect_subgroups
nodes.summary: Detects communities/subgroups in the interaction network via greedy modularity clustering on the undirected projection.

nodes.name: plot_network_graph
nodes.summary: Draws the interaction network with node sizing driven by a chosen metric, spring layout, edge-width scaling by weight, and a titled legend.

nodes.name: plot_network_dashboard
nodes.summary: Composes the multi-panel network dashboard: centrality metric bars, strongest pairs, interaction patterns, and subgroup composition.

nodes.name: analyze_network
nodes.summary: Pipeline convenience wrapper: builds the interaction graph and computes metrics, key participants, patterns, and subgroups into one result dict.

nodes.name: identify_conversation_starters
nodes.summary: Marks conversation starters using a time-gap threshold (default 60 minutes) with a date-change fallback, adding is_conversation_starter and prev_sender columns to the sorted frame.

nodes.name: calculate_initiator_ratio
nodes.summary: Computes per-sender conversation-initiation counts plus a balance ratio showing who starts chats more often, with the most frequent initiator flagged.

nodes.name: analyze_response_patterns
nodes.summary: Derives responder/response-time statistics per participant and per directed pair — count, mean, median, spread — and identifies the fastest and slowest responders.

nodes.name: calculate_dominance_scores
nodes.summary: Scores each sender's dominance from message count, message length, and conversation-control components with normalized weighting.

nodes.name: calculate_relationship_health_score
nodes.summary: Blends initiator, responsiveness, and dominance components (documented weights, responsiveness 35%) into the overall relationship health score with grade and per-component breakdown.

nodes.name: _rolling_window_score
nodes.summary: Multiprocessing worker that computes the relationship health score for one rolling-window chunk of dates.

nodes.name: _collect_health_scored
nodes.summary: Collects and sorts the scored window results returned from the process pool into a single frame.

nodes.name: _date_row_spans
nodes.summary: Precomputes start/end row offsets per date so rolling windows can slice the frame without rescanning it for every window.

nodes.name: _rolling_window_fast
nodes.summary: Vectorized fast path for rolling-window health scoring: reuses daily aggregates and per-window slices to compute each date's health score without recomputing full metrics per window.

nodes.name: calculate_rolling_health_score
nodes.summary: Public rolling-health API: validates window and minimum-message parameters, dispatches to the fast path or the parallel fallback, and returns the per-date health-score frame.

nodes.summary: Fallback dashboard implementation used when the enhanced visualization path is unavailable, plotting initiator, response, and dominance panels.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: README.md is the front door to chat-analyzer-pro: a Python 3.11+ tool that turns a WhatsApp .txt, Telegram .json, or .zip chat export into terminal insights plus a single self-contained offline HTML report — one command, entirely on your machine, with no accounts, uploads, or telemetry. It introduces the project's central design idea: an always-on feature tier every install gets, versus an optional [nlp] extra that adds 6-class emotion classification and a generative narrative. It also covers the quickstart with bundled samples, privacy guarantees, and the environment-variable configuration table — the vocabulary the rest of this tour builds on.

tour.title: Architecture Map
tour.description: Before diving into code, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md gives you the map: an ASCII pipeline diagram (parsers → ingest → analysis → adapter → HTML report), a complete inventory of the src/chat_analyzer modules, and the data contract boundary that separates them. It also records the key design decisions — CLI-first Typer, lazy heavy imports, the [nlp] gate, opt-in result cache, and the single-file HTML report. Keep this diagram in mind: every later step fills in one block of it.

tour.title: Packaging & Feature Tiers
tour.description: pyproject.toml operationalizes the tier idea from Step 1: the core dependency set (pandas, typer, rich, matplotlib, networkx, vaderSentiment, reportlab) stays lean, while the optional [nlp] and [dev] extras carry the heavy machine-learning dependencies. It also declares the chat-analyzer console script, wheel packaging for the vendored ECharts assets, and the pytest slow marker used by the test suite. Note how the packaging file already encodes architecture: what installs by default determines what the code can import eagerly.
tour.languageLesson: PEP 621 'extras' let one package advertise optional dependency groups — installing with `pip install 'chat-analyzer[nlp]'` pulls the extra group only when asked. That is how the lean base install avoids shipping torch and transformers to everyone.

tour.title: CLI Entry Point
tour.description: The journey from typing a command to running analysis starts here: __main__.py enables `python -m chat_analyzer` and raises SystemExit with the Typer app, while cli/__init__.py exposes that same app as the console-script target declared in pyproject.toml in Step 3. cli/main.py then performs the orchestration a user sees — validating WhatsApp/Telegram export paths, resolving the NLP tier through an interactive menu or environment override, and driving the pipeline, HTML report generation, and report auto-open with friendly, never-traceback errors. This chain is also the codebase's natural reading order: a dependency BFS from __main__.py reaches exactly these files first (nlp_gate.py sits one hop further, waiting in Step 9).
tour.languageLesson: Python entry points: __main__.py makes a package runnable with `python -m`, while a [project.scripts] entry maps a console command straight to a Typer app object. Typer reads type-annotated function parameters to generate argument parsing, help text, and validation automatically.

tour.title: Raw Export Parsing
tour.description: Building on the entry point from Step 4, the parsing layer turns raw chat exports into normalized data. ingestion.py is the dispatcher for every supported input — WhatsApp .txt, Telegram-style JSON, ZIP archives, screenshots via OCR, and PDFs with an OCR fallback — normalizing raw messages into the canonical message schema with honest skip counting. The two specialists beneath it do the format-specific work: whatsapp_parser.py regex-matches both bracketed and plain timestamp layouts and classifies system/media lines, while telegram_parser.py handles bare-chat and full-export JSON shapes, recursively joins entity-array texts, and filters service messages. The bundled samples — whatsapp_sample.txt with its emoji and <Media omitted> lines, and telegram_sample.json — are exactly the demo inputs the README quickstart replays.

tour.title: Canonical Data Contracts
tour.description: Follow one message from the sample export and you land in the schema shown by data/processed/example_parsed.csv: one row per message with datetime, sender, text, date, time, hour, and message_length — the canonical DataFrame every analysis module expects. cli/contracts.py formalizes the wider interface: the ParseReport dataclass aggregating parse counters and the AnalysisResults TypedDict describing the complete analysis payload, which keeps the analysis core CLI-agnostic. cli/adapters.py then acts as the single anti-corruption layer, adapting each analysis module's raw result dicts into that typed contract with defensive .get() access so empty edge cases never raise. This contract is the shared vocabulary the pipeline (next step) and the HTML report both speak.
tour.languageLesson: Python's TypedDict gives a plain dict a static type contract: keys of AnalysisResults are checked by type checkers while the value stays a JSON-serializable dictionary — ideal for data that must cross from pandas stages into HTML templates.

tour.title: Pipeline Orchestration
tour.description: cli/pipeline.py is the busiest node in the whole graph — 24 outgoing dependencies, 8 incoming — the single place where a run comes together. run_pipeline detects the input type (WhatsApp, Telegram, or ZIP), parses it into the canonical DataFrame from Step 6, then drives every analysis stage in order: EDA, sentiment, relationship health, network, chart specs, narrative, emotion, and Tier-B summarization, before mapping results into the AnalysisResults contract. zip_input.py handles the third input format's trickier half: enumerating .txt/.json transcripts inside a WhatsApp/Telegram archive, letting the user pick on a TTY, and merging every chosen transcript into one ParseReport-compatible result so run_pipeline itself needs no changes downstream.

tour.title: Always-On Analysis Engine
tour.description: These five modules are the analysis engine every install gets without any NLP download. ChatEDA in eda.py enriches the canonical DataFrame with time features and computes volume, activity, dynamics, and content statistics; sentiment.py layers VADER, TextBlob, and an optional HuggingFace model with spawn-safe parallel scoring; relationship_health.py adds conversation starters, response lag, dominance, a rolling-window health score, and the gamified friendship index; network_graph.py builds directed sender-to-sender reply graphs and computes centrality and community metrics. narrative.py rounds out the tier — a Tier A, always-on layer that turns basic statistics into hedged, clearly-disclaimed observations using only pandas and regex, with no torch dependency. Each optimized path here is guarded by parity tests proving vectorized results match a straightforward reference implementation — a discipline Step 12 extends to the whole pipeline.

tour.title: NLP Environment Gate
tour.description: The heavy NLP tier from Step 3 never loads eagerly — cli/nlp_gate.py is the checkpoint that decides whether it can run at all. It verifies pinned package versions and cached Hugging Face models, exposes the tier's knobs (emotion sample cap, worker count, result cache), and installs or downloads what is missing with a Windows long-path guard around pip and the model cache. scripts/make_nlp_env.ps1 is the concrete workaround behind that guard: it creates a disposable NLP venv at a short TEMP path to dodge Windows MAX_PATH crashes (WinError 206) in deeply nested environments. result_cache.py completes the environment story with the opt-in disk cache whose key mixes the chat file hash, app version, and NLP/sampling configuration — so re-running an unchanged chat skips the expensive stages entirely.
tour.languageLesson: Windows historically caps paths at 260 characters (MAX_PATH), and deeply nested virtualenvs blow past it with WinError 206. The PowerShell helper sidesteps the limit by creating the venv under a short TEMP path — no registry changes needed.

tour.title: Generative NLP Modules
tour.description: These are the two heavyweights the gate from Step 9 unlocks. emotion.py performs six-class classification (joy, sadness, anger, fear, surprise, love) with a HuggingFace DistilBERT pipeline, scaling to huge chats via deterministic stratified sampling above a 50,000-message cap, process-pool parallel exact scoring, and opt-in INT8 quantization. summarizer.py drives T5-based abstractive conversation summarization with group-chat support — whole-conversation, date-range, and per-participant summaries plus key-topic extraction and dominant-speaker detection. Per the project's privacy design, the generative narrative side of this tier reads only a derived-stats digest and never the raw chat text, keeping machine-learning models away from private conversations.

tour.title: Self-Contained HTML Report
tour.description: Everything computed in Steps 7–10 funnels into one HTML file. cli/chart_json.py builds JSON-serializable ECharts specifications — daily timeline, activity heatmap, participant bars, sentiment and health trends, a 3D network layout, plus emotion pie and quarterly-timeline specs. cli/report_html.py renders the report card itself: an autoescape Jinja2 template with tabbed panels, boundary-validated chart PNG data URIs, and inline-scrubbed vendored ECharts bundles, written to a sanitized filename in the working directory with best-effort browser auto-open. The vendored assets are so central they carry their own license files — Apache 2.0 for ECharts and BSD 3-Clause for echarts-gl, whose drag-to-rotate 3D network view needs the GL build — and the fact that they are inlined is what makes the report work fully offline.

tour.title: Golden Parity Testing
tour.description: How do you trust an analyzer that keeps rewriting its own hot paths? tests/golden holds two long-format metric,value CSVs — expected aggregates for the WhatsApp and Telegram sample fixtures (27 parsed messages, avg_compound 0.503544 for WhatsApp) captured from real tier-1 pipeline runs. test_golden_parity.py re-runs the actual pipeline on those committed samples and asserts every projected metric matches, so a fresh clone verifies the entire parse-EDA-VADER path in seconds without downloading any NLP models. This is the regression baseline that makes the optimization claims from Steps 8 and 9 checkable.

tour.title: CI Quality Gate
tour.description: The GitHub Actions workflow in .github/workflows/ci.yml runs three parallel jobs: a lean pytest matrix across ubuntu/windows and Python 3.11/3.12, a slow CLI/e2e suite with a ruff lint pass, and an NLP job proving the optional [nlp] extra actually installs — with in-progress runs on the same ref cancelled. docs/TESTING.md maps the whole 330-test suite: the runnable command matrix, the per-area coverage table linking every test file to the feature it exercises, the D-17 mocking conventions, and how the suite splits across those three CI jobs. Finishing the tour here closes the loop: the tiered, parity-tested architecture you walked through is exactly what this matrix protects.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions YAML: the `on` trigger decides when a workflow runs, jobs run in parallel by default (the three-job split here), and steps within a job run sequentially. A concurrency key can cancel superseded in-progress runs on the same branch.
